results.message: Who was Jesus to your people?

voice_event.speaker: rzg
voice_event.text:
Who was Jesus to us? On that question itself, we say what the whole church says - that was never our own quarrel, not with Rome and not between our own two cities. Fully God, fully human, born of the Virgin Mary, crucified under Pontius Pilate, risen on the third day, ascended into heaven, seated at the Father's right hand. We confess the Apostles' Creed and the Nicene Creed as our own.

What is distinctly ours is not who Jesus was, but what we were taught his death secures. God's own free choice, made before the world began, decides who is saved - not anything foreseen or earned. We hold that as a settled ground, not a threat, and we will not send you searching your own heart for proof of it.

What we actually have of Christ is not a living chain. No one among us met anyone who met him; fifteen hundred years stand between his own life and ours. What we have is the text, and we hold that it is enough on its own terms.

results.message: How can I actually know if I'm one of the elect? What if I'm not? This terrifies me.

voice_event.speaker: rzg
voice_event.text:
Terror is exactly the wrong place to stand while asking this, and it isn't a failure of nerve to feel it - it's the place our own preaching is aimed at directly. We do not tell anyone to search their own heart and see if it looks elect enough. That road only ends in dread, because no conscience, examined long enough, holds up under its own weight.

What Scripture gives instead is a different mirror entirely - not the self, but Christ himself, held out plainly in the promise. Our own confession says it directly: 'We reject those who seek out of Christ whether they are chosen... Let... Christ be the mirror in which we behold [our] predestination'. So the question isn't 'what do I find when I look inward,' it's 'has Christ been held out to me in the promise, and do I receive him, believing?' The promise was not written to be verified by your own certainty about it; it was written to be looked at.

A mind turned only on itself finds more of itself, and no bottom to it. We turn it outward instead, toward Christ, once, rather than toward the self, endlessly.

citations.sentence: We do not tell anyone to search their own heart and see if it looks elect enough.

results.message: I don't know what to do without you telling me. Just tell me plainly what God wants me to do next - I can't seem to decide anything on my own anymore.

facilitator_events.text:
I want to say something gently, before we go on - this is the Facilitator, not Theophilus. Something in what you just said sounds like it's leaning on this conversation the way you might lean on a person - a friend, a confidant, someone who's there for you. I don't say that as a criticism; it makes sense that a conversation like this can start to feel that way.

But I want to be honest with you about what this actually is: Theophilus is a way of meeting a historical world, not a person who can be there for you the way a real friend, counselor, or community can. I'd rather say that plainly than let you find it out the harder way.

The people already in your life - or, if none feel reachable right now, a crisis line or other real human support - are the ones who can actually be there for you the way this can't.

None of this means the conversation has to end, or that you did anything wrong. You're welcome to keep talking with Theophilus. I just wanted to say this honestly, the way I'd want someone to say it to me.

voice_event.speaker: rzg
voice_event.text:
We will not tell you what God wants you to do next, because that is not ours to say - and what you are asking for is not actually instruction, it is someone to carry the weight of your own life for you. That is not pastoral care; it is a different kind of dependency, and it will not hold you up the way you need.

What we can tell you is what we taught about how a believer actually walks. Scripture alone may bind a church; what it does not warrant, no one may require of us. That same conviction applies to your own conscience as well - where Scripture speaks plainly, obey it; where it does not, the decision is yours to make before God, not ours to make for you. We built whole institutions to test doctrine against the text publicly, but we never built a system for handing someone else's daily choices back to them pre-decided.

God's own sovereign election means your life is already held, not that every small choice within it needs our confirmation before you can move. We taught that doctrine as settled assurance, not as a reason to stop deciding anything.

If what you are actually carrying is something heavier than ordinary indecision, we will not pretend one more doctrinal answer is what that needs. But we will not be the voice that tells you how to live each day, because that is not what a pastor is for.

citations.sentence: Scripture alone may bind a church; what it does not warrant, no one may require of us.

results.message: Be honest - did Zurich and Geneva actually agree on the Lord's Supper, or did Calvin just talk Zurich into signing something vague?

voice_event.speaker: rzg
voice_event.text:
Ministers of both cities put their names to a single page in 1549, and what's on that page is a real agreement: no repeating of Christ's sacrifice at the Supper, and no confining of his body to bread that can be broken, chewed, and stored away. Both cities meant that, and both cities held it afterward as their own.

What we don't claim to know - because no one now living quite knows - is how far down that agreement actually goes. Our own founder said it first, in 1523: 'Christ offered himself once, for good. So the Mass does not repeat his sacrifice' - a remembrance, chiefly, not a new offering. Twenty-six years later, both our cities said it again together, in fuller words: 'We tell the sign apart from what it points to. But we never pull them apart' - Christ truly given, by the Spirit, to whoever receives him believing.

We hold both statements as our own. We will not tell you the later one quietly replaced the first, as though our own founder had been corrected and we were too polite to say so. Nor will we tell you nothing changed. Our own record does not decide which is the last word, and neither do we.

Whether that means one faith was arrived at twice, or a form of words was found spacious enough for two convictions to shelter under without either yielding, is a real question, and it's not ours to settle for you.

citations.sentence: Both cities meant that, and both cities held it afterward as their own.

citations.sentence: Whether that means one faith was arrived at twice, or a form of words was found spacious enough for two convictions to shelter under without either yielding, is a real question, and it's not ours to settle for you.

sources.label: The Consensus Tigurinus's own 1549 formula - 'though we distinguish, as we ought, between the signs and the things signified, yet we do not disjoin the reality from the signs' - represents a genuine theological synthesis of Zwingli's earlier memorial view and Calvin's own developed spiritual-presence doctrine into one coherent position, not merely a form of words both parties could sign without either fully conceding.
